Think & Gather · About the Club

Why we
gather.

We made Think & Gather because being around people is not the same thing as connecting with them — and talking is not always the same thing as having a conversation.

01 / THE BEGINNING

An alternative to the feed.

Most of us are rarely bored anymore. There is always another thing to watch, read, scroll past, save for later, or send to someone.

That abundance can be useful. It can also make life strangely passive. We consume other people’s ideas all day without always making much room for our own. We know what everyone is doing, but not necessarily what they’re thinking about.

Think & Gather was created as a small counterweight to that. A reason to leave the house, put the phone away, sit with people you may not know yet, and spend a couple of hours actually engaging with something.

Not every gathering needs to be profound. Some will be playful. Some will be ridiculous. Some might change your mind. The point is simply to create the conditions for conversations that go a little further than the usual script.

02 / WHAT WE'RE MAKING

A social club with something to talk about.

Every month has a different premise. A debate gives us something to disagree about. A murder mystery gives us something to solve. Speed learning gives everyone five minutes to become the most interesting person in the room about one very specific thing.

There will be books, films, shared meals, creative nights, questions, and formats we haven’t thought of yet. Think & Gather isn’t an academic club, and you do not need to be an expert in anything.

You just need to be interested enough to ask another question.

What matters
in the room.

The club is private and intentionally small because the quality of a gathering changes when people feel comfortable enough to participate, disagree, ask something half-formed, or admit they don’t know.

I

Go past the small talk.

You can ask what someone does. Just don’t stop there.

II

Be interested.

The best person in the room does not need to be the one with the most answers.

III

Disagree well.

A different opinion is an invitation to understand how someone got there.

IV

Put the phone down.

Not because phones are bad. Because the conversation in front of you deserves a chance.

V

Leave room to change your mind.

Certainty is not the price of admission.

03 / WHO IT'S FOR

Curious is enough.

Think & Gather is for people who like learning things they have no practical reason to know. People who ask follow-up questions. People who miss dinner tables where everyone forgets what time it is.

You do not need the right résumé, the right vocabulary, or the right opinion. You just need to come willing to take part.
